caption:
Solar Words, Straight #3: BYOD Plus. Hawaiian Electric pays you upfront to enroll your battery. Here's what you're agreeing to. Sources on the last slide.

Follow for more plain-English Oʻahu solar math.

#Oahu #HawaiiSolar #SolarPower #HawaiianElectric #Honolulu

slides.text: HECO will pay you $400 per kW for your battery. Here's the trade.

slides.label: per kW you commit, paid once, upfront. Income-qualified homes get another $400 per kW.
a month in HECO's own example: a credit for the energy your battery sends to the grid.
slides.sub: Varies by rate. Older NEM customers don't get it.

slides.text: The trade: your battery works for the grid 2 hours a day, every day.
slides.sub: You pick the window. It powers your home first, then sends the rest out.

slides.text: Leave early? You pay back part of the upfront money.
slides.sub: 60 days' notice, prorated. Check your term: HECO's page lists 5 years in one place and 10 in another.
“How many kW should I commit, and how much battery is left for my evenings and outages?”

slides.text: Follow for straight answers on Oʻahu solar.

items: Hawaiian Electric, Bring Your Own Device Plus program page (hawaiianelectric.com), viewed Nov 19, 2026: $400/kW upfront, $400/kW LMI adder, one 2-hour daily window, 60-day notice and prorated repayment, example monthly credit ~$52.
